name: abnormal and post-menopausal bleeding overview
title: Abnormal uterine bleeding divided by age: reproductive age split by the exam into structural (PALM) or functional (COEIN) causes, adolescence and perimenopause, and post-menopausal bleeding worked up in three steps to the biopsy report that picks atrophy, hyperplasia or carcinoma; each column gives clues, numbered investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB): divide by AGE first
lines: any change in frequency, duration or amount of flow, or bleeding between cycles
every one: is she STABLE? vitals first · β-hCG (pregnant: see the FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart)

groups.title: REPRODUCTIVE AGE: does the EXAM find a lesion?
lines: treat the cause; otherwise regulate the bleeding: medicines → minimally invasive (embolization, ablation) → hysterectomy

groups.title: POST-MENOPAUSAL: any bleeding after 12 months without menses

pres.title: Work up in order
lines: 1 · Exam with a SPECULUM: a negative Pap test does not end it
2 · Transvaginal ultrasound: endometrium < 5 mm is normal
3 · ENDOMETRIAL BIOPSY if > 5 mm, or bleeding recurs · HYSTEROSCOPY for a focal lesion or a failed biopsy
the biopsy report picks the column ↓

head: h
Structural: PALM
Polyp · Adenomyosis · Leiomyoma (fibroid) · Malignancy + hyperplasia
clue: mass at the os · ENLARGED uterus (fibroid, adenomyosis) · FIXED (cancer)

head: h
Functional: COEIN
Coagulopathy · Ovulatory · Endometrial · Iatrogenic · Not yet classified
clue: stress, weight, exercise · thyroid, prolactin · polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
bruising, petechiae · galactorrhea, hirsutism, thyroid signs · hormones she takes
inv: 2 · TSH, prolactin · FSH, LH, estradiol · androgens
tx: OCP · Depo · Mirena · Visanne · GnRH agonist

head: h
Adolescence
immature axis: 2 years to regular cycles
clue: COAGULOPATHY: menarche can unmask von Willebrand

head: h
Perimenopause
usually anovulation, but MALIGNANCY is more common
clue: ask about her cycles: one arrest had a hemoglobin of 38
tx: fluids, ABCs, blood · Foley tamponade · IV Premarin · operating room if it fails
estrogen + progesterone, or progesterone · TXA · avoid invasive surgery

head: h
Atrophy
the MOST COMMON cause
tx: vaginal cream, pill or ring · nothing if not bothered

head: h
Endometrial carcinoma
#1 gynecologic malignancy
clue: 1: estrogen-driven, like hyperplasia · 2: serous, older, atrophic background

panels.title: Choosing a hormonal agent
items: Depo, Mirena: sustained, but an injection or a device
Lupron: fast and effective, but side effects and cost
TXA: as needed, cuts how heavy, not how often
